newsitem.title: CUBA: Small explosion in Havana hotel-witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Small explosion in Havana hotel-witnesses.

text.p: A small explosion, possibly caused by a bomb or firework, damaged the lobby of central Havana's top hotel early on Monday, witnesses said.

Dutch tourist Roberto Koppens told reporters he arrived in the lobby of the Melia Cohiba hotel several minutes after an explosion and saw smoke, minor damage to furnishings, and could smell gunpowder.
The explosion at the Cohiba came just three weeks after two bombs rocked the lobbies of two other Havana hotels, the Nacional and the Capri, causing damage but no injuries.

Officials at the Cohiba, which is owned by the Cuban state firm Cubanacan and managed by Spanish hotel chain Sol Melia, declined to comment on the incident, which took place at about 7.30 a.m. (1130 GMT).

The director of Cubanacan, Juan Jose de la Vega, visited the hotel during the morning but declined to confirm there had been a bomb or firecracker. Pressed by reporters outside the hotel, he said "it was a lot of noise". He said nobody was injured.
Part of the lobby of the tower block hotel was sealed off with a wooden partition and workmen could be heard hammering. It was not possible to see the damage behind the screen.
